question.text:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X \sim N(-4,1^2),$ compute $P(X \lt -4.47).$

$z$ $\, 0.05 \,$ $\, 0.06 \,$ $\, 0.07 \,$
$\, -0.6\,$ $\,0.2578 \,$ $\,0.2546 \,$ $\,0.2514 \,$
$\, -0.5 \,$ $\,0.2912 \,$ $\,0.2877 \,$ $\,0.2843 \,$
$\, -0.4 \,$ $\, 0.3264 \,$ $\, 0.3228 \,$ $\, 0.3192 \,$
question.explanation:
Given a normal random variable $X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2),$ we have

\[ P(X \lt x) = P \left( Z \lt \dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma} \right) \]

where $Z \sim N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu = -4$ and $\sigma = 1.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

\begin{align*} P(X \lt -4.47) &= P \left( Z \lt \dfrac{-4.47-(-4)}{1} \right) \\[5pt] &= P(Z \lt -0.47) \\[5pt] &= P(Z \leq -0.47) \\[5pt] &= \Phi(-0.47) \end{align*}

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

According to the table, we have

\[ \Phi(-0.47) = 0.3192. \]

Therefore, we conclude that

\[ P(X \lt -4.47) = 0.3192. \]

$z$$\, 0.00 \,$$\, 0.01 \,$$\, 0.02 \,$
$\, -0.7 \,$ $\, 0.2420 \,$ $\, 0.2389 \,$ $\, 0.2358 \,$
$\, -0.6 \,$ $\, 0.2743 \,$ $\, 0.2709 \,$ $\, 0.2676 \,$
$\, -0.5 \,$ $\, 0.3085 \,$ $\, 0.3050 \,$ $\, 0.3015 \,$
question.explanation:
Given a normal random variable $Y \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2),$ we have \[ P(Y \geq y) = P \left( Z \geq \dfrac{y-\mu}{\sigma} \right) \] where $Z \sim N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu = -2$ and $\sigma = 4.$

First, we transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring: \begin{align*} P(Y \geq -4.48) &= P \left( Z \geq \dfrac{-4.48-(-2)}{4} \right) \\[5pt] &= P(Z \geq -0.62). \end{align*}

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} P(Z \geq -0.62) &= 1 - P(Z \lt -0.62) \\[5pt] &= 1 - P(Z \leq -0.62) \\[5pt] &= 1 - \Phi(-0.62). \end{align*}

From the table, we know that \[ \Phi(-0.62) = 0.2676. \]

Therefore, we have \begin{align*} P(Z \geq -0.62) &= 1 - \Phi(-0.62)\\[5pt] &= 1 - 0.2676 \\[5pt] &= 0.7324. \end{align*}

Finally, we conclude that \[ P(Y \geq -4.48) = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0.7324}. \]

question.explanation:
Given a normal random variable $X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2),$ we have

\[ P(a \lt X \lt b) = P \left( \dfrac{a-\mu}{\sigma} \lt Z \lt \dfrac{b-\mu}{\sigma} \right) \]

where $Z \sim N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu = 6$ and $\sigma = 3.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

\begin{align*} P(7.26 \lt X \lt 8.85) &= P \left( \dfrac{7.26 - 6}{3} \lt Z \lt \dfrac{8.85 - 6}{3} \right) \\[5pt] &= P( 0.42 \lt Z \lt 0.95 ). \end{align*}

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} P(0.42 \lt Z \lt 0.95) &= P(Z \lt 0.95) - P(Z \leq 0.42) \\[5pt] &= P(Z \leq 0.95) - P(Z \leq 0.42) \\[5pt] &= \Phi(0.95) - \Phi(0.42). \end{align*}

From the table, we have the following:

\begin{align*} \Phi(0.95) &= 0.8289 \\[3pt] \Phi(0.42) &= 0.6628 \end{align*}

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} P(0.42 \lt Z \lt 0.95) &= \Phi(0.95) - \Phi(0.42) \\[5pt] &= 0.8289 - 0.6628 \\[5pt] &= 0.1661. \end{align*}

Finally, we conclude that

\[ P(7.26 \lt X \lt 8.85) = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0.1661}. \]

\begin{align*} P(-1.3 \lt Z \lt -0.28) &= \Phi(-0.28) - \Phi(-1.3) \\[5pt] &= 0.3897 - 0.0968 \\[5pt] &= 0.2929. \end{align*}

\[ P(-5.9 \lt X \lt -2.84) = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0.2929}. \]

example.title: Computing the Probability of a Normal Random Variable on a Bounded Interval

question.text:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X \sim N(-3,10^2),$ compute $P(-0.7 \lt X \lt 16.3).$ Use the tables below and do not round your answer.

$z$$\, 0.02 \,$$\, 0.03 \,$$\, 0.04 \,$
$\, 0.2 \,$ $\, 0.5871 \,$ $\, 0.5910 \,$ $\, 0.5948 \,$
$\, 0.3 \,$ $\, 0.6255 \,$ $\, 0.6293 \,$ $\, 0.6331 \,$
$\, 0.4 \,$ $\, 0.6628 \,$ $\, 0.6664 \,$ $\, 0.6700 \,$
$z$$\, 0.03 \,$$\, 0.04 \,$$\, 0.05 \,$
$\, 1.8 \,$ $\, 0.9664 \,$ $\, 0.9671 \,$ $\, 0.9678 \,$
$\, 1.9 \,$ $\, 0.9732 \,$ $\, 0.9738 \,$ $\, 0.9744 \,$
$\, 2.0 \,$ $\, 0.9788 \,$ $\, 0.9793 \,$ $\, 0.9798 \,$
question.explanation:
Given a normal random variable $X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2),$ we have

\[ P(a \lt X \lt b) = P \left( \dfrac{a-\mu}{\sigma} \lt Z \lt \dfrac{b-\mu}{\sigma} \right) \]

where $Z \sim N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu = -3$ and $\sigma = 10.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

\begin{align*} P(-0.7 \lt X \lt 16.3) &= P \left( \dfrac{-0.7 - (-3)}{10} \lt Z \lt \dfrac{16.3 - (-3)}{10} \right) \\[5pt] &= P( 0.23 \lt Z \lt 1.93 ). \end{align*}

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} P(0.23 \lt Z \lt 1.93) &= P(Z \lt 1.93) - P(Z \leq 0.23) \\[5pt] &= P(Z \leq 1.93) - P(Z \leq 0.23) \\[5pt] &= \Phi(1.93) - \Phi(0.23). \end{align*}

From the table, we have the following:

\begin{align*} \Phi(1.93) &= 0.9732 \\[3pt] \Phi(0.23) &= 0.5910 \end{align*}

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} P(0.23 \lt Z \lt 1.93) &= \Phi(1.93) - \Phi(0.23) \\[5pt] &= 0.9732 - 0.5910 \\[5pt] &= 0.3822. \end{align*}

Finally, we conclude that

\[ P(-0.7 \lt X \lt 16.3) = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0.3822}. \]

question.text:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X \sim N(-1,4),$ compute $P(1.64 < X < 4.4).$

$z$$0.01$$0.02$$0.03$

$z$$0.00$$0.01$$0.02$

$\, 2.8 \,$ $0.9974$ $0.9975$ $0.9976$

question.explanation:
Given a normal random variable $X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2),$ we have

\[ P(a < X < b) = P \left( \dfrac{a-\mu}{\sigma} < Z < \dfrac{b-\mu}{\sigma} \right) \]

where $Z \sim N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu = -1$ and $\sigma = \sqrt 4 = 2.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

\[\begin{align*} P(1.64 < X < 4.4) &= P \left( \dfrac{1.64-(-1)}{2} < Z < \dfrac{4.4 - (-1)}{2} \right) \\[5pt] &= P( 1.32 < Z < 2.7 ) \end{align*}\]

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)\mathbin{:}$

\[\begin{align*} P(1.32 < Z < 2.7) &= P(Z < 2.7) - P(Z \leq 1.32) \\[5pt] &= P(Z \leq 2.7) - P(Z \leq 1.32)\\[5pt] &= \Phi(2.7) - \Phi(1.32) \end{align*}\]

From the table, we have the following:

\[\begin{align*} \Phi(1.32)&= 0.9066\\[3pt] \Phi(2.7) &= 0.9965 \end{align*}\]

Therefore, we have

\[\begin{align*} P(1.32 < Z < 2.7) &= \Phi(2.7) - \Phi(1.32)\\[5pt] &= 0.9965- 0.9066 \\[3pt] &= 0.0899. \end{align*}\]

Finally, we conclude that

\[ P(1.64 < X < 4.4) = 0.0899. \]
